observer: Claude (Opus 5.5), 9 Nov 2026: the raw scan (2984 x 2242) blurred 3x3, overview and a tile of the pillar with a 0.02 grid; the consoles were not read, this inventory is of the pillar and the sheet and its wiring only
covers: the cab's right side from the driver's seat, looking right: the structure of the right pillar and the pressed sheet beside it, with the lower sill; no part of the roof is in frame
notes: VEHICLE: the hangar session, the ex-NVA 9A33BM3-1 (g082-g096). No roof is visible in this photo; it is listed for the pressed panels and the pillar only. Forward is image left. The sheet at x 0.49-0.72 has the same soft, wrinkled-looking painted skin as the roof's surface in g089-a and g089-b, which suggests the coat is a general finish on the cab's sheet, not padding only where it shows wrinkles. The wrinkles here are in a plain wall panel beside the A-2 box, so it is unlikely to be cushion padding.

details.what: the right pillar: a pale grey-green pressed channel from the top of the frame to the sill, a deep flange on its right edge, its near face holding the plate and the black plate at its top
details.size_cue: about as wide as the black plate on it

details.what: the pillar's flange joint, a dark vertical line and a lighter strip between the channel and the panel on its right
a thin grey wire down the pillar in a loose curve with clips, into a hole in the sill at the foot
a round hole in the pillar below the plate with a thin wire entering it
the wall panel to the right of the pillar: bare-looking grey sheet with soft blotchy wrinkles and white streaks, a pressed texture, unpadded
a thin blue wire run along the panel's left and bottom edge, in white band clips, turning under to the A-2 box
a straight tube rail or shelf edge across the top of the wall panel, steel, from the pillar to the right edge, wing nuts toward its right end
details.size_cue: about as thick as the pillar's flange

details.what: a heavy horizontal fold at the bottom of the panel, the wall stepping out over the lower box: dirty and scuffed along its edge
a white-edged vertical joint down the panel's right side: a pale strip and a hinge or latch at the panel's top, the next panel beyond
the sill's paint: heavily worn and blackened by feet and hands near the pillar's foot, in a broad patch
